target_customer: Patients in underserved settings (primary and specialty care, street medicine) and health plans and payers that fund their care
problem: Healthcare capacity is limited and slow to reach people. Akido builds AI (ScopeAI) that expands clinician capacity and runs its own medical network.
business_model: Full stack AI native medical provider network (Akido Medical/Care) billing payers, with ScopeAI as its core technology

founders.name: Jared Goodner
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Prashant Samant
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and named CEO by SiliconANGLE in May 2025. One search result says the company grew out of the USC Digital Health Lab and names Sanjit Mahanti and Hugh Gordon as additional founders, unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: Clinical AI decision support combined with running a medical practice network. The founding product is not described in opened sources.

defensibility.rationale: A provider network, payer contracts and clinical data accumulate over time, though the early company's product is unknown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acting against Akido. It was independent in 2026.

market_need_then: The founding era need is not documented in opened sources. In 2025 coverage the company cites access gaps, with its own page citing 26 day average lead times for visits.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven healthcare and AI language

rebrands.why: Positioned as an AI native health system, dropping Labs (reported by a trade outlet)

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage of funding and an ethics council, with no evidence of broader brand recognition. Search results are polluted by similarly named Aikido and Akedo companies.

pivots.to: Full stack provider with its own medical network
pivots.why: Reported by a trade outlet in a search result; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Akido, founded in 2015 and part of YC's winter 2015 batch, moved from software to running its own care network and raised a 60 million dollar Series B led by Oak HC/FT in May 2025, citing about half a million patients. The company went about a decade before this raise, so the success factors rest on a pivot toward a full stack provider and the AI tailwind. Early history and earlier rounds are thinly documented.
notes: Series B cross-checked in search results by Fenwick, Pulse 2.0 and Newcomer. Totals conflict: $60.8M over 8 rounds (CB Insights), $25M raised before Series B (one outlet), $109.2M and $84.25M (other trackers). An aggregator lists an $11.2M Series A with Mission and Market and Future Communities Capital, unverified. CB Insights lists a December 2023 acquisition of Rhode Island Primary Care Physicians by Akido, not verified. The company site was fetched but gave no founding story or founders. The first product at founding was not found, so no dated competitors are listed.
